description: Figure 6(a) is a grouped vertical bar chart illustrating how the number of datasets changes by year for researcher locations, showing the five most frequent locations plus an “Other” category. The horizontal axis contains the categories as years labeled from 2012 through 2022 in chronological order, and the vertical axis is labeled “Number of datasets” on a logarithmic scale with tick marks at approximately 10^0, 10^1, and 10^2. Each year displays multiple narrow, side-by-side colored bars corresponding to the legend “Researcher Location”: Other (blue), USA (orange), IN (green), UK (red), IT (purple), and DE (brown). Early years (2012–2015) show only small bars near 1–2 datasets (notably orange USA bars around 2 and occasional blue Other bars around 1–2), while from 2016 onward more locations appear each year with values spanning roughly from about 1 up to near 10^2; for example, the tallest blue “Other” bar occurs around 2021 at approximately 100 datasets, and the orange “USA” bars reach into the tens (roughly ~40–60 at their highest around 2021), with UK/IT/DE/IN bars generally in the single digits to tens depending on year (e.g., several around ~5–20 in 2019–2022). The bars are grouped by year rather than sorted by magnitude, and there is no special visual emphasis such as outlines or annotations beyond the legend and axis labels.
